examples.en: A small rest area was built in the park.
While hiking, I drank water at a rest area.
The elderly gather at the village rest area and chat.

examples.ko: 이 쉼터는 누구나 무료로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can use this rest area for free.
We looked for a rest area and went into the shade.
The rest area in the middle of the road was clean too.

explain: 공원, 산길, 도로 옆처럼 잠깐 쉬어 가도록 만든 곳에 써요. 건물 안에서 쉬는 공간은 '휴게실'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I rested a while at the rest area on the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쉼터'와 '쉬다'가 같은 말뿌리라서 자연스럽게 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 쉼터 and 쉬다 share a root, so they pair naturally.
phrases.en_equiv: to rest at a rest area

phrases.en: There is a small rest area by the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 나타내는 말과 함께 장소를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a size word to describe the place.

phrases.en: The city hall built a rest area in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉴 수 있는 곳을 새로 지을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for building a new place to rest.

explain_en: It is used for places made for a short rest, such as a park, a mountain trail, or the side of a road. A resting space inside a building is called 휴게실.

examples.en: How can your voice be this pretty?
Maybe it will rain tomorrow.
How are you so good at cooking?
Perhaps he has arrived by now.

examples.ko: 어쩜 말도 없이 그냥 가 버렸어요?
examples.en: How could he just leave without a word?

examples.ko: 어쩜 제 생각이 틀릴 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Maybe my thinking could be wrong.

explain: 어쩜은 '어쩌면'의 줄임말처럼 쓰여서 '아마 그럴지도 몰라요'라는 느낌을 줘요. '어쩜 이렇게 예쁠까'처럼 놀라거나 감탄할 때도 써요. 이때는 뒤에 '이렇게', '그렇게'가 자주 와요.

phrases.en: Perhaps it might snow tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어쩜'의 원래 말이고, 말할 때와 글에서 모두 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of '어쩜', natural in both speech and writing.

phrases.en: How can it be this delicious?
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 눈앞의 것에 놀라거나 감탄할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express amazement at something right in front of you.

phrases.en: How can you be so kind?
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대나 다른 사람의 모습에 감탄할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express admiration at another person's manner.

explain_en: 어쩜 works as a short form of '어쩌면' and gives the feeling of 'perhaps'. It is also used to express surprise or admiration, as in '어쩜 이렇게 예쁠까'. In that use, '이렇게' or '그렇게' often follows.

examples.en: Walking alone on a night road feels dangerous.
Don't play risky pranks.
The child was sitting on the railing, which looked dangerous.
The driving felt dangerous.

examples.ko: 그 계획은 조금 위험스러울 것 같아요.
examples.en: That plan seems a bit risky.
It looked dangerous, so I didn't go near it.

explain: '위험하다'는 사실로 위험한 것, '위험스럽다'는 위험해 보이거나 그렇게 느껴진다는 말이에요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '위험스러워요', '위험스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 말할 때는 '위험해 보여요'도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 눈이 오는 날 산길은 위험스러운 길이에요.
phrases.en: A mountain road on a snowy day is a dangerous-looking road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '위험스럽다'가 '위험스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, 위험스럽다 changes to 위험스러운.

phrases.en: This ride isn't so dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험해 보이지 않는다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something does not seem dangerous.

phrases.en: That bridge looks a bit dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위험스럽다'와 비슷한데 말할 때 더 자연스럽고 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 위험스럽다 but more natural and easier in speech.

explain_en: Something looks or feels a bit dangerous (위험스러워 보이다) The plain adjective states that something is actually dangerous, while this one says it looks or feels dangerous. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so the ending changes in forms like the polite present and the modifier. In speech, 'it looks dangerous' is also common.

en: to be taken advantage of; to be exploited (by someone)

examples.ko: 저는 친구에게 이용당한 것 같아서 슬퍼요.
examples.en: I feel sad because it seems my friend used me.

examples.ko: 그는 사람들에게 이용당해도 화를 내지 않았어요.
examples.en: He didn't get angry even when people used him.
If you do not want to be used by others, refuse clearly.
Very naive people get used easily.
I felt the company was using me, so I quit my job.
I read contracts carefully so I won't be taken advantage of.

explain: 남이 자기 이익을 위해 나를 쓴 불쾌한 경험을 말해요. 단순히 서비스를 쓰는 '이용하다'나 중립적인 '이용되다'와 달라요. '무시당하다', '사기당하다'처럼 '-당하다'가 붙은 말은 보통 나쁜 일에 써요.

phrases.en: I found out later that my friend had used me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 나쁜 일을 겪었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense: you already went through the bad experience.

phrases.en: I don't want to be used by anyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶지 않다'로 원하지 않는 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-고 싶지 않다' expresses not wanting it to happen.
phrases.en_equiv: I don't want to be used

phrases.en: I feel like that person used me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '느낌이 들다'와 함께 쓰면 확실하지 않아도 그렇게 느낀다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '느낌이 들다', it means you feel that way even if you're not certain.

explain_en: It describes the unpleasant experience of being used by someone for their own benefit. It differs from plain '이용하다' (using a service) and the neutral '이용되다'. Verbs ending in '-당하다', like '무시당하다' and '사기당하다', are normally used for bad things.

examples.en: I move into a new apartment next month.
Our family moved in last week.
I went today to see the house I will move into.
I greeted the neighbor who just moved in.
Once the date is set, I want to move in right away.
The construction was delayed, so we could not move in.

explain: 입주하다는 새로 지은 아파트나 오피스텔처럼 새 건물에 들어갈 때 어울려요. 보통 집에서 집으로 옮길 때는 '이사하다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The residents' meeting is tomorrow evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 건물이나 단지에 들어와 사는 사람들을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The people who move into and live in a new building or complex.

phrases.en: The move-in date has been set for March 1st.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새집에 들어가는 날을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the day you move into a new home.

phrases.example: 내년 봄에 새 아파트에 입주할 예정이에요.
phrases.en: I plan to move into the new apartment next spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 들어갈 계획을 말할 때 '-(으)ㄹ 예정이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -(으)ㄹ 예정이다 to talk about a planned move-in.

explain_en: Moving into a new home or building as a resident (아파트에 입주하다) Ipjuhada fits when you move into a newly built apartment or office-tel. When you just move from one home to another, 'isahada' sounds more natural.

examples.en: Many curious animals live in the jungle.
The explorers went into the jungle.
The jungle is hot and humid, so it's hard to walk.
The child likes movies set in the jungle.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 정글의 길이 진흙으로 변해요.
examples.en: When it rains, the jungle paths turn to mud.

examples.ko: 정글에서 길을 잃은 사람을 구조대가 찾았어요.
examples.en: The rescue team found the person who got lost in the jungle.

explain: 정글은 열대 지방의 나무가 빽빽한 숲이에요. 일반적인 숲은 '숲'이나 '산림'이라고 해서 달라요. '콘크리트 정글'처럼 도시를 빗대어 말할 때도 있어요.

phrases.example: 방학에 정글 탐험을 해 보고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to go on a jungle expedition during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정글'과 자주 같이 쓰는 짝말로, 모험 이야기에 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing with 정글, often seen in adventure stories.

phrases.en: It is dangerous if you get lost in the jungle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 나타내는 '에서'와 함께 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sentence pattern that uses 에서 to mark the place.
phrases.en_equiv: to get lost in the jungle

phrases.example: 서울은 높은 건물이 많아서 콘크리트 정글 같아요.
phrases.en: Seoul has many tall buildings, so it feels like a concrete jungle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 숲이 아니라 건물이 가득한 도시를 빗대어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is figurative and describes a city full of buildings, not a real jungle.

explain_en: 정글 is a dense tropical forest. An ordinary forest is '숲' or '산림', so they differ. It can also be used figuratively for a city, as in '콘크리트 정글'.

examples.en: A singing contest is being held at school.
My friend won a prize at a photo contest.
I also want to enter this contest.
The contest starts next Saturday.
I was busy preparing for the cooking contest.
There are many singers who became famous through contests.

explain: 비슷한 말로 '대회'가 있어요. 운동 경기에는 '대회'가 자연스럽고, 콘테스트는 노래, 요리, 사진처럼 솜씨를 겨루는 분야에 어울려요.

phrases.en: There is a cooking contest next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '콘테스트'와 비슷한 말이고, 운동 경기에도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that also works naturally for sports events.

phrases.en: I want to enter the photo contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회에 참가한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to take part in a contest.

phrases.example: 동생이 노래 콘테스트에서 일 등 했어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling won first place in the singing contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the result.
phrases.en_equiv: to win first place in a contest

explain_en: A similar word is 대회. For sports, 대회 sounds more natural, while 콘테스트 fits skill-based fields like singing, cooking, and photography.

en: to be unified; to become uniform

examples.en: The two countries become one.
The uniforms in our class are now uniform.
Once the opinions are unified, we start right away.

examples.ko: 글꼴이 통일된 발표 자료가 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: Presentation materials with a uniform font look good.
The method has not been unified yet.
I hope the method will be unified by next week.

explain: 한국에서는 남한과 북한의 '통일'이 큰 주제라서 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 표, 글꼴, 의견처럼 서로 달랐던 것이 하나로 맞춰질 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The students' opinions have not been unified yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 의견이나 규칙이 아직 하나가 아니라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means different opinions or rules are not yet made one.

phrases.en: I want to live in a unified country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통일된'은 하나가 된 것을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes something that has become one.

phrases.example: 남북이 통일되면 기차로 유럽에 갈 수 있을 거예요.
phrases.en: If the two Koreas unify, we could go to Europe by train.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면'을 붙여 앞으로의 일을 상상할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-(으)면' to imagine future possibilities.

explain_en: Opinions, rules or styles become the same; also national unification. In Korea, the unification of South and North Korea is a big topic, so the word appears often in the news. It is also used when different tables, fonts or opinions are brought into line.
